semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَبُرَ مَقْتاً}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it belongs to the chapter of niʿma and biʾsa (verbs of praise and blame), so that «كَبُرَ» contains a vague latent pronoun explained by the indefinite noun after it. «وأَنْ تقولوا» is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), and so the well-known disagreement arises regarding it: is its nominative ending by virtue of being a mubtadaʾ, with its khabar being the clause preceding it, or is its khabar omitted, or is it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as was set out earlier. This is a regular rule: every verb at which wonder (taʿajjub) is permissible may be built on the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn, and it follows niʿma and biʾsa in all rulings. The second is that it is one of the forms of wonder. Ibn ʿUṣfūr counted it among the wonder constructions given a chapter in grammar, saying: "The form mā afʿalahu, afʿil bihi, and la-faʿula, such as لَرَمُوَ الرجل." Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: "This is among the most eloquent speech and the most expressive in its meaning. By «كَبُرَ» he intended wonder, though not in its own wording, as in his saying:
4256 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . .
غلَتْ نابٌ كُلَيْبٌ بَواؤُها
(How costly became the she-camel Kulayb's equivalent!)
Then he said: "It was predicated of «أَنْ تقولوا», and «مَقْتاً» was put in the accusative as its explanation, indicating that their saying what they do not do is pure hatred, with no admixture in it." The third is that «كَبُرَ» is neither for wonder nor for blame, but is predicated of «أَنْ تقولوا», and «مَقْتاً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from agency, the original being: كَبُرَ مَقْتُ أَنْ يقولوا, that is, "the hatred of your saying grew great." It is also possible that the agent is a latent pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from his saying «لِم تقولونَ», that is, "it grew great", meaning the saying, "in hatred"; and «أَنْ تقولوا» on this view is either a badal (substitute) for that pronoun, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is "it is that you say". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُقاتَلون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, in the passive. «يُقَتَّلون» was also read, with shadda.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {صَفّاً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "in ranks" or "drawn up in ranks".
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُم}: it may be a second ḥāl from the agent of «يُقاتِلون»; it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «صَفّاً», in which case it is a nested ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila); al-Zamakhsharī said this. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of «صَفَّاً»; al-Ḥawfī said this. The pronoun returned to «صَفّاً» in the plural because it is a plural in meaning, as in His saying {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]. As for «المَرْصُوص», it was said: that whose parts are fitted together and level. It was also said: that which is bound with lead. It was also said: it is from close-packing, from the tight set of the teeth (tarāṣṣ al-asnān). Al-Rāʿī said:
4257 - ما لَقِيَ البيضُ من الحُرْقوصِ ... يَفْتَحُ بابَ المُغْلَقِ المَرْصوصِ
(What the fair ones have suffered from the ḥurqūṣ, which opens the door of the shut, tightly-fitted [place].)
الحُرْقوص is a small crawling creature that is fond of virgin women.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَقَد تَّعْلَمُونَ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya).

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مُّصَدِّقاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise «مُبَشِّراً»; the governor is «رسول» because it has the sense of "one sent" (al-mursal). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask, by what are «مُصَدِّقاً» and «مُبَشِّراً» put in the accusative: by the sense of sending contained in «الرسول», or by «إليكم»? I say: by the sense of sending; because «إليكم» is a ṣila of «الرسول», so it cannot govern anything, since prepositions do not govern by themselves but by the verbal sense they contain; so when they occur as ṣilas that do not implicate a verbal sense, from where would they govern?" End. By his saying "ṣilas" he means that they are attached to «رسول» as a connection to it, that is, their meaning is connected with it, not the technical ṣila. «يأتي مِنْ بعدي» and «اسمُه أحمدُ» are two clauses in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; or «اسمُه أحمدُ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَأْتي»; or the first is a naʿt and the second a ḥāl. That the two be ḥāls is weak because they come from an indefinite, although Sībawayh permits it. «أحمدُ» may be a transfer from the imperfect verb or from the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), the apparent one being the second. On either view it is barred from the ṣarf (is a diptote) because of being a proper name and the predominant verbal pattern, except that on the first it is barred when definite and takes tanwīn when indefinite, while on the second it is barred whether definite or indefinite, since the adjectival quality replaces the proper-name quality. When it is made indefinite after having been a proper name, the disagreement between Sībawayh and al-Akhfash arises, which is a well-known question among the grammarians. Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him, recited, praising the Prophet ﷺ, and he gave it tanwīn:
4258 - صلَّى الإِلهُ ومَنْ يَحُفُّ بعرشِه ... والطيبونَ على المباركِ أحمدِ
(God blessed, and those who surround His throne, and the pure ones, the blessed Aḥmad.)
«أحمد» is a badal or a bayān (explicative apposition) of «المبارك».
His saying: {هذا سِحْرٌ}: the disagreement of the readers regarding it has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida.
And the Shaykh said here: "The majority read «سِحْرٌ», while ʿAbd Allāh, Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Wathāb read «ساحر»," and he omitted mention of the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī].

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ يدعى إِلَى الإسلام}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of «افترى»; this is the reading of the majority. Ṭalḥa read «يَدَّعي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and shadda on the dāl, in the active, and there are two interpretations of it. One is that of al-Zamakhsharī, namely that yafta ʿilu is in the sense of yafʿalu, like لَمَسَه and التمَسه. The two pronouns, I mean «هو» and the latent one in «يَدَّعي», refer to Allah the Exalted, and then the two readings are of one meaning, as if it had been said: "and Allah calls to Islam." In the first reading the two pronouns refer to «مَنْ». The second is that it is from ادَّعى كذا دَعْوَى, but since «يَدَّعي» was made to imply the sense of "to belong to, to be affiliated with", it was made transitive with «إلى», otherwise it is transitive by itself; and on this view the two pronouns are also for «مَنْ», as in the well-known reading.
From Ṭalḥa also: «يُدَّعى» with shadda on the dāl, in the passive. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it according to what was said before: ادَّعاه and دَعاه are of one meaning, like لَمَسه and التمَسه. The two pronouns refer to «مَنْ», the reverse of what he held in explaining the first reading, in which the two pronouns refer to Allah the Exalted, as was set out earlier.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لِيُطْفِئُواْ}: there are several possibilities regarding this lām. The first is that it is added (mazīda) to the object of "wanting". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its original is: they want to extinguish (yurīdūna an yuṭfiʾū), as came in Sūrat al-Tawba. It is as if this lām was added to the verb of wanting for emphasis, because of the sense of wanting in it, as in your saying «جِئتُ لأكرمَك», just as the lām was added in «لا أبالك» to emphasize the sense of iḍāfa in «لا أباك»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The lām in «لِيُطْفِئوا» is an emphasizing lām that entered the object, for the implied form is: they want to extinguish. This lām most often accompanies the object when it is fronted. You say: «لزيدٍ ضَرَبْتُ» and «لِرؤيتِك قصَدْتُ»." End. This is not the position of Sībawayh and most people. Moreover, Abū Muḥammad's saying "most often accompanies..." to the end is not apparent, because no one says it is obligatory at all; rather its addition is permissible, and it is also not the case that its addition is the more frequent; rather its absence is more frequent.
The second is that it is the lām of cause, and the object is omitted, that is: they want to nullify the Qur'ān, or repel Islam, or destroy the Messenger, peace be upon him, in order to extinguish.
The third is that it has the sense of the subjunctive «أَنْ», and that it governs the verb itself. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs put the lām of purpose (lām kay) in the place of «أَنْ» with arāda and amara"; and al-Kisāʾī too held this. A similar case was given for you in His saying {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ} in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ [verse 26].
His saying: {مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ḥafṣ and Ibn Kathīr read it with «مُتِمُّ» in iḍāfa to «نورِه»; the rest read it with tanwīn and «نورَه» in the accusative. The iḍāfa is a lightening, and the tanwīn is the original. The Shaykh disputes that it is the original, as was given earlier. His saying «واللَّهُ متمُّ» is a circumstantial clause from the agent of «يريدون» or «يُطفئوا»; and his saying «ولو كَرِه» is a ḥāl from this ḥāl, so the two are nested. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, that is, "He would complete it and make it prevail", and likewise {وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الكافرون}.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {تُنجِيكُم}: the clause is a ṣifa (qualifier) of «تجارة». Ibn ʿĀmir read «تُنْجِّيكم» with shadda; the rest read it lightened, from أَنْجى. The two are of one meaning, because doubling and the hamza both make a verb transitive.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {تُؤْمِنُونَ}: it has no grammatical position, because it is an explanation of «تجارة». It is also possible that its position is nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "that commerce is: you believe", the khabar being the same as the mubtadaʾ so there is no need for a link (rābiṭ); or that its position is accusative through an implied verb, that is, "I mean: you believe". That is permissible on the assumption of «أَنْ», though it involves strain. The majority have «تُؤْمنون» as a khabar in form, with the nūn retained. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] has «آمِنوا» and «جاهِدوا» as two imperatives. Zayd ibn ʿAlī has «تؤمنوا» and «تجاهِدوا» with the nūn of the nominative dropped. As for the reading of the majority, the khabar is in the sense of an imperative, to which the two irregular readings point; for the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī rests on the omission of the lām of command, that is: «لِتؤمنوا ولتجاهِدوا», as in his saying:
4259 - محمدُ تَفْدِ نَفْسَك كلُّ نفسٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Muḥammad, let your soul be ransomed, every soul...)
and His saying {قُل لِّعِبَادِيَ الذين آمَنُواْ يُقِيمُواْ} [Ibrāhīm: 31] on one view, that is, «لِتَفْدِ» and «ليقيموا»; and for that reason the verb is jussive in its apodosis in His saying «يَغْفِرْ». Likewise their saying: «اتقى اللَّهَ امرؤ فَعَلَ خيراً يُثَبْ عليه», its implied form being: «ليتقِ اللهَ». Al-Akhfash said: "«تؤمنون» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of «تجارة»." This cannot be imagined except by the interpretation that the original was «أنْ تؤمنوا», and when «أن» was dropped the verb became nominative-ending (marfūʿ), as in his saying: 4260 - ألا أيُّهذا الزَّاجِريْ أَحْضُرُ الوغَى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who forbid me to attend the battle...) The original is «أن أَحْضُرَ». It is as if it were said: "Shall I direct you to a saving commerce: faith and striving?" This is a good meaning, were it not for the interpretation it involves. On this view it can be a badal from «تجارة». Al-Farrāʾ said: it is jussive as the answer to the question, which is His saying «هل أدلُّكم». The people differ on whether this statement is sound: some of them held it to be mistaken. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is not that when He directs them to what benefits them, He forgives them; He forgives them only if they believe and strive." He means that it is not consequent upon the mere question, nor upon the mere direction. Al-Mahdawī said: "It is sound only by construing it according to the meaning: that «يؤمنون» and «يُجاهدون» are an ʿaṭf bayān on His saying «هل أدلُّكم», as if the commerce were not known, what it is, and so it was clarified by faith and striving, it being the two of them in meaning; so it is as if it were said: 'Do you believe and strive?'" He said: "If you do not assume this implied form, it is not sound, because it becomes: 'if you are directed, He will forgive you,' whereas forgiveness becomes obligatory only by acceptance and faith, not by direction." Al-Zamakhsharī said something close to this as well. He also said: "«تُؤْمنون» is resumptive, as if they said: 'How shall we act?' and He said: 'You believe.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«تُؤْمنون» is a verb with nominative ending, its implied form being: ذلك أنَّه تُؤْمنون," so he made it the khabar of «أَنَّ», and it and what is in its sphere are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. This is to be taken as an explanation of the meaning, not an explanation of the i'rāb, since there is no need for it.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {يَغْفِرْ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is jussive as the apodosis of a khabar in the sense of a command, as was set out earlier. The second is that it is jussive as the answer to the question, as al-Farrāʾ said, and its interpretation was given earlier. The third is that it is jussive by an implied condition, that is: "if you believe, He will forgive you."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وأخرى}: there are five possibilities regarding it. The first is that it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with its khabar implied, that is, "and for you", or "there", or "with Him is another quality (khaṣla)", or "another reward". And «تُحبُّونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of it. The second is that the khabar is a clause whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being: "it is victory", the clause being the khabar of «أُخْرى»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and it is very far-fetched, because it is an implied form for which there is no need. The third is that it is accusative through an omitted verb indicated by the context, that is, "and He will give you" or "He will grant you another reward". And «تُحبونها» is a naʿt of it also.
The fourth is that it is accusative through an implied verb explained by «تُحبُّونها», so that it is a case of ishtighāl (preoccupation), and then «تُحِبُّونها» is not a naʿt, because it explains the governor before it. The fifth is that it is genitive by ʿaṭf on «تجارة». This was weakened on the ground that it is not among what the commerce pointed to; it is only a reward from Allah. This view is reported from al-Akhfash.
His saying: {نَصْرٌ مِّن الله}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "that blessing, or the other bond (khalla), is victory." And «من الله» is a naʿt of it, or attached to it, that is, its beginning is from Him. The nominative ending of «نصرٌ» and «فتحٌ» is the reading of the majority; Ibn Abī ʿAbla put the three in the accusative. There are several possibilities in that, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī. The first is that they are accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification). The second is that they are accusative as maṣdars, that is: they are given victory, and a near conquest is opened for them. The third is that they are accusative as a badal from «أُخْرى», while «أُخْرى» is accusative by an implied verb, as before, that is: "He will forgive you, admit you to gardens, and give you another," and then he substituted for it «نَصْراً وفَتْحاً قريباً».

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {أَنصَارَ الله}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «أنصاراً» with tanwīn and «لله» as a preposition and its genitive noun. The rest read «أنصارَ» without tanwīn, in iḍāfa to the noble Name. The orthography allows both readings. The lām may be added (mazīda) to the object for reinforcement, since the governor is derivative [of a verb], the original being: أنصاراً اللَّهَ; or it may be not added, the preposition and its genitive noun being a naʿt of «أَنْصاراً»; the first is clearer. As for the reading with iḍāfa, it derives from the aforementioned original. What supports the reading with iḍāfa is the consensus on it in His saying {نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ الله}. A disagreement here cannot be conceived because it is written with an alif.
His saying: {كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى}: there are several possibilities. The first is that the kāf is in the position of accusative with an implied "saying", that is: "We said that to them, as ʿĪsā said." The second is that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "Be a being", as Makkī said, and there is room for objection, since they are not commanded to be a being. The third is that it is speech understood by its meaning rather than its wording, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it, for he said: "If you ask, what is the validity of the comparison, when its apparent sense is a comparison of their being helpers with the saying of ʿĪsā, blessings of Allah upon him, «مَنْ أنصاري»? I say: the comparison is understood by the meaning, and on that it is sound; the intended sense is: 'Be helpers of Allah as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā, when he said to them: {مَنْ أنصاري إِلَى الله}.'
The transitivity of «أَنْصَاري» with «إلى» was given in Āl ʿImrān, along with the differences of the people about it. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying {مَنْ أنصاري إِلَى الله}? I say: its meaning must correspond to the disciples' reply: «نحن أنصارُ الله». What corresponds to it is that the meaning be: 'Who is a soldier of mine, turning toward the support of Allah?' The iḍāfa of «أَنْصاري» is different from the iḍāfa of «أنصار الله»; for the meaning of «نحن أنصارُ الله» is: 'We are those who help Allah', and the meaning of «مَنْ أنصاري» is: 'Who are the helpers who are devoted to me and will be with me in the support of Allah?' It is not sound for its meaning to be 'who will help me together with Allah', because that does not correspond to the reply. The proof of this is the reading of those who read «أنصارَ الله»." End. I say: he means that some claim that «إلى» is in the sense of «مع», that is, "Who are my helpers with Allah?" And his saying "the reading of those who read «أنصارَ الله»" means: if it were in the sense of «مع», its omission would not be sound in this reading. This is not necessarily so, because every reading has a meaning of its own, though it is preferable that the two readings agree.
His saying: {فَأَيَّدْنَا الذين آمَنُواْ على عَدُوِّهِمْ}: it is a case of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun in both, to draw attention to the disbeliever's enmity toward the believer; for the original is: «فأيَّدْناهم عليهم», that is, "We supported the believers against the disbelievers of the two groups mentioned."
